questions.question: How does a cashback site make money to pay you?
options: It shares the commission retailers pay it when you buy via its link
questions.explanation: Retailers pay commission and the site passes part of it to you.

questions.question: To make sure cashback tracks, you should…
options: Click through from the cashback site and accept cookies
Buy through the retailer's app directly
questions.explanation: Tracking relies on cookies. Ad blockers and some extensions can break it.

questions.question: Using a voucher code that isn't listed on the cashback site can…
questions.explanation: Many retailers decline cashback when unauthorised codes are used.

questions.question: Cashback marked “pending” means…
options: The retailer hasn't confirmed it yet, which can take weeks
questions.explanation: Pending cashback can still be declined.

questions.question: Which of these commonly gets cashback declined?
questions.explanation: No sale, no commission, no cashback.

questions.question: A £400 laptop: 3% from a cashback site plus 1% from a cashback card. Total back?
Buy a £60 supermarket gift card at 5% back. You earn…
What's a sensible rule with gift card cashback apps?
options: Only buy for shops you'll definitely spend at, and spend it fairly soon
questions.explanation: Unused balances, or a retailer going bust, can lose you money.

questions.question: Why compare two cashback sites before buying?
options: Rates for the same shop can differ
questions.explanation: One site may pay double the other for the same retailer.

questions.question: Cashback is best treated as…
options: A bonus that's only real once it's paid out
questions.explanation: Don't spend it until it lands.

questions.question: Buying something you don't need just to get cashback…
options: Still costs more than not buying it
questions.explanation: 10% back on something you didn't need is still 90% spent.

questions.question: Why might a cashback site pay a different rate for the same shop next week?
questions.explanation: Rates move, so check on the day you buy.

questions.question: “Double cashback” offers are best used when…
options: You were going to buy the item anyway
questions.explanation: A boost doesn't help if it makes you spend more than you planned.

questions.question: A £120 jacket: 8% cashback, or a 10% voucher code that would void the cashback. Which is better?
options: The voucher: £12 off now vs £9.60 later
questions.explanation: £12 off now beats £9.60 that might take weeks or be declined.

questions.question: Cashback is usually NOT paid on…
questions.explanation: Most retailers pay commission on the goods, not the delivery.

questions.question: Which is better: a 10% voucher on £120 now, or 8% cashback later?
questions.explanation: A 10% voucher saves £12 now, while 8% cashback is £9.60 later. Take the bigger, more certain saving.

questions.question: Someone asks you to pay a bill in gift cards. What is it?
questions.explanation: Anyone who asks you to pay a bill, fine or tax in gift cards is a scammer.

questions.question: What is one risk of holding unused gift card balances?
options: They can be lost if the retailer goes into administration
questions.explanation: Unused balances can be lost if a retailer goes into administration, and some cards expire.

questions.question: What does 'stacking' mean?
options: Getting more than one saving on the same purchase
Buying lots of the same item
questions.explanation: Stacking combines separate layers of saving, such as a sale price, cashback and loyalty points, on one purchase.

questions.question: You use a voucher code that the cashback site does not list. What often happens?
questions.explanation: Many cashback sites decline cashback when you use an unlisted voucher code, so check the shop's terms first.

questions.question: A cashback credit card stacks with a cashback site because…
options: The card is only how you pay
questions.explanation: The cashback site tracks your click, and the card is just the payment method, so the two usually work together.

questions.question: You buy a £40 item you didn't need, with 10% cashback. What have you done?
options: Spent £36 net on something you didn't need
questions.explanation: Cashback only helps on things you would have bought anyway. Otherwise you have just spent money.

questions.question: What should you do before you click through to a shop from a cashback site?
options: Start with an empty basket and one shop tab
questions.explanation: TopCashback says an empty basket, one shop tab and no VPN or ad blocker give the best chance of tracking.

questions.question: You place two separate orders from one cashback click. What is the risk?
options: The second order may not track
questions.explanation: Each order needs its own click through the cashback site.

questions.question: Two cashback or voucher browser extensions are active together. What can happen?
options: One overrides the other and cashback is lost
questions.explanation: Use one at a time. Competing extensions can overwrite the click that your cashback depends on.

questions.question: Quidco says to raise a missing cashback claim within how many days of purchase?
questions.explanation: Quidco's help page says to raise a claim within 45 days of purchase, and after at least 72 hours. Check the current page.

questions.question: What do you need to raise a missing cashback claim?
questions.explanation: A screenshot of the confirmation with the shop, order reference, date and total is what the claim form asks for.

questions.question: Cashback shows as 'pending'. How should you treat it?
options: Don't count it until it is paid
questions.explanation: Pending cashback can be declined or delayed. Count it only once it has landed.

questions.question: You return a cashback purchase. What usually happens to the cashback?
questions.explanation: Returns and cancellations normally cancel the cashback on that order.

questions.question: You carry a balance on a cashback credit card. What often happens to the reward?
questions.explanation: Reward cards often charge higher rates, so interest can cost more than you earn.

questions.question: What is the safe way to use a cashback credit card?
options: Set a Direct Debit for the full balance
questions.explanation: Clear it in full every month and use it only for normal spending, never for cash withdrawals.

questions.question: Section 75 on a credit card covers items priced…
questions.explanation: The limit is per item. A part-payment on the card can bring the whole cost under cover.

questions.question: You see a 1% cashback card with a spending cap and a rate that drops after a year. Check…
options: The terms before relying on the headline rate
questions.explanation: Introductory rates and caps change, so read the current terms.

questions.question: A retailer enters administration. What may happen to your gift card?
options: It may stop being accepted or only cover part of an order
questions.explanation: Administrators can stop accepting gift cards or limit them, so spend the balance quickly.

questions.question: You paid for a gift card by credit card, and the retailer fails. What may help?
options: A Section 75 claim with your card provider
A phone call to the shop
questions.explanation: You may be able to claim from your card provider, depending on the item price and the circumstances.

questions.question: Which test should you use before stacking?
questions.explanation: If you would not buy it anyway, no amount of stacking makes it a saving.
